description: Independent audit findings for the frozen MC-18 internal bilingual landing at ca64ec7. Severities are BLOCKING/MAJOR/MINOR/INFORMATIONAL; the recommendation is limited to the internal landing scope and is not a programme verdict, publication approval or WCAG conformance statement. External legal/commercial/hardware approvals are recorded as limitations, not implementation defects.
generationMethod: Independent audit executed in the frozen worktree at ca64ec7f9f079326321cc7070ad2b1acf2832bc9: diff inspection, npm run test:landing (56/60), npm run test:landing:unit (45/45), 37 independently reproduced adversarial mutations, tsc app+preview, preview build/probe, Playwright landing suite (44/44), public build isolation probe, screenshot SHA-256 verification, data re-derivation, content/evidence/parity checks and document-vs-code cross-check.
knownLimitations: External approvals do not exist and are not MC-18 implementation defects: trademark clearance NOT_GRANTED and public use NO_GO, source-IP/licensing not cleared, legal identity not verified, no approved price or stock, no selected hardware, no conformity/CE/NMEA 2000/CRA evidence, no SLA, PILOT safety gate BLOCKED, no customer evidence, no WCAG conformance, no Search Console/hosting/TLS evidence.
The 13 MC-14 release gates are open (0 closed) and 24 required documents are unexecuted; publication remains NOT_AUTHORIZED and LANDING_RELEASE_AUTHORIZATION is null.

Accessibility evidence is automated axe only (Chromium, no serious/critical violations, one color-contrast incomplete per run); no screen reader, manual WCAG 2.2 AA or non-Chromium verification was executed.
Visual baselines were generated and compared by the same QA run and were not reviewed by a second human; 5 of 8 repeat captures are not byte-identical and are disclosed with both hashes.
Performance evidence is a single lab run over loopback without throttling or field data and asserts no thresholds.
Hydration is proven in Chromium only on the development preview configuration; the preview is loopback-only, not a public host.
The preview serves / as a documented developer alias inside the loopback preview; it is not listed in preview-isolation.json previewOnlyRoutes and is not a public route.
Documents D01/D02/D08/D09/D14 still quote authoring-time counts (55/60, format:check exit 1, uncommitted worktree); D23 must record the frozen-state values. This is recorded as MC18-IR-01.

findings.evidence: At the frozen commit the validator reports 56/60 (not 55/60), npm run format:check exits 0 (not 1), HEAD is committed ca64ec7 and src/app contains only newly added landing files (not an uncommitted or empty diff), and the SSR byte counts are 316,049/313,958 (not 315,629/313,904). The affected documents quote authoring-time observations, not the frozen state.
findings.reproduction: Run npm run test:landing, npm run format:check, git rev-parse HEAD, git diff --name-only 6002c49..HEAD -- src/app, and HTTP probes against the freshly built preview.
findings.requiredCorrection: D23 must record ca64ec7 and the frozen command results and explicitly supersede these authoring-time snapshots; alternatively update D01/D02/D08/D09/D14 before delivery. No source change required.
findings.owner: docs-a (documents group A) + Lead for D23

findings.evidence: The evidence descriptor says the canonical dataset establishes PAGE_MAREA_OVERVIEW, but docs/marea/information-architecture/data/proposed-routes.json items[0].pageType is HUB_OVERVIEW and models/page-identity.ts correctly uses HUB_OVERVIEW. D09 §2 already records the inconsistency as informational; validator MC18-45 passes because the typed identity is correct, not because the evidence text is.
findings.reproduction: Read evidence.ts and the generated content-evidence.json; run node -e over proposed-routes.json to print items.find(r => r.routeId === 'mareaOverview').pageType (HUB_OVERVIEW).
findings.requiredCorrection: Change the establishes text to HUB_OVERVIEW (optionally noting the master-prompt label) and regenerate with npm run build:landing:data, or explicitly annotate the master-prompt label inside the string. Do not edit the canonical MC-15 dataset.

findings.evidence: app.listen(port, host, ...) is top-level, outside the if (isMainModule(import.meta.url)) block, which is empty. npm run build:landing:preview prints the runtime banner 'MC-18 internal landing preview (NOT PUBLISHED): http://127.0.0.1:4302/marea', proving the Angular build evaluates the server entry and reaches app.listen during the build. The build still exits 0 on this Windows host (duplicate-bind tolerance), but on a host that does not tolerate a second bind the build can fail with EADDRINUSE when 4302 is occupied.
findings.reproduction: With port 4302 free, run npm run build:landing:preview and observe the startup lines in the build output; node dist/marea-landing-preview/server/server.mjs still serves correctly.
findings.requiredCorrection: Move app.listen(...) and its log lines inside the existing isMainModule guard (keep the reqHandler export). Isolation behaviour is otherwise correct.

findings.evidence: The preview serves / as a developer alias for the ES landing (documented in D02 §2.2 and D08 §3.2 and covered by the same loopback/Host/noindex controls), but previewOnlyRoutes lists only /marea and /en/marea. This is a documentation/data-completeness gap, not a publication risk: the alias is loopback-only, noindexed and never mounted in the public application.

findings.requiredCorrection: None required for internal scope; if the alias is kept, add it to the isolation dataset as a documented developer alias in a future data regeneration.
